text: Not every accounting entry fits neatly inside a regular period. Year-end audit adjustments and final true-ups often need a period of their own, set apart from ordinary activity. That's the adjusting period.

A period type, like Month or Week, is the category of regular period a calendar is built from. Every regular period in a calendar shares the same type — a monthly calendar has twelve month-type periods.

An adjusting period is a special, additional period layered onto the regular calendar for entries that shouldn't appear in normal operating balances — year-end audit adjustments, attached after the last regular month.
Most companies define just one adjusting period, at fiscal year-end. Some 13-period calendars define more than one, but extra adjusting periods mean extra complexity to maintain.

Oracle Fusion lets reports include or exclude adjusting period activity depending on the question being asked — pre-audit versus post-audit numbers. Next up, lesson seventeen: currencies and conversion rate types.
